answer: One concrete Sybil defence is stake-bonded pairing: each identity posts collateral locked for a fixed term and forfeited if it is caught controlling a second one. An agent enters at a summit of the reputation graph, vouched by two unrelated peers whose own bond is slashed if the claim is false. This makes a fake cluster an expensive oasis rather than free signups: every extra identity adds capital at risk, and the whole ring stands on onyx-hard surety that collapses once detected.
